demuxer.wav.notes: Finite little-endian RIFF/WAVE linear/G.711 PCM only. Packet boundaries are budget-dependent; RF64/BW64/RIFX, other compressed audio, streaming unknown sizes, multiple data chunks and metadata extraction are unimplemented. Strict malformed-input checks can differ from native FFmpeg. Scoped CLI timing follows pinned default PCM packet boundaries; input seeking at/beyond EOF is explicitly unsupported pending native I/O fallback compatibility.

muxer.wav.notes: Finite linear/G.711 PCM WAV output with known sample count, bounded sequential writes and transactional output contract. Contiguous zero-based sample timestamps required. RF64, unknown-length output, arbitrary timestamp gaps, metadata and other compressed codecs are unimplemented. Headers need not be byte-identical to FFmpeg.

decoder.pcm_u8.notes: Packed PCM only. Integer depth conversion, integer/float conversion and float precision conversion are partial. Float-to-integer CLI requires -cpuflags 0 and finite values with magnitude <= 32768; SIMD/default dispatch, non-finite/out-of-range integer conversion, cross-precision NaN payloads, resampling and channel remix remain incomplete. Scoped default s16/flt/dbl FIR rate conversion accepts supported PCM/G.711 input/output formats with native internal precision selection. Fixed-profile and selected default u8/s16 domain fixtures are byte-exact; the 1600-case raw matrix and integer container/time/filter cases have explicit numerical contracts. Complex filter graph placement, combined rematrix, non-default resampler options and general conformance remain incomplete. Supported linear mixed-precision volume/FIFO/asetrate rate conversion now executes at the negotiated format boundary with numerical differential evidence; complex graphs and combined rematrix remain incomplete. Finite FIR semantic packet schedules now cover output frame limits, seek-clipped first frames, positive sub-sample output duration and framecrc independently of physical I/O chunks. Bounded bigint cumulative queries represent startup allocation overflow, zero-output packets and 4096-sample drains. Native evidence: 248 count-plan scenarios, 1152 numerical limit/timing cases, 384 silent framecrc scenarios under two budgets, 144 nonzero fixed-point framecrc cases and 144 container-input cases, plus local workerd. General floating checksum identity and extreme bounded-rational approximation remain unverified.
